title: A Comprehensive In-Silico Pipeline for the Discovery of Non-toxic, Stable Antimicrobial Peptides From Databases for Targeting Multi-Drug Resistant K. pneumoniae.
authors: Dev Sharma, Pranab; Noman, Abdullah Al; Talukder, Md Al Amin; Parvez, Md Jakaria; Hafiz, Md Al; Nath, Bratakatha; Sharma, Himanshu
one_liner_zh: 该研究用计算流程筛选抗菌肽靶向K. pneumoniae的DnaA蛋白，涉及蛋白-DNA对接和分子模拟，但对象是抗菌肽-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA体系，方法可迁移但深度有限。
abstract: The rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae has significantly reduced the effectiveness of conventional antibiotics, highlighting the need for alternative therapeutic strategies. This study employed a comprehensive in silico pipeline to identify antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) targeting the essential DNA replication initiator protein DnaA. A total of 28,361 peptide sequences were collected from publicly available AMP databases and sequentially filtered based on peptide length, net charge, GRAVY score, instability index, antimicrobial activity, toxicity, hemolytic potential, aggregation propensity, sequence similarity and favorable amphipathic properties. Four peptides satisfied all selection criteria and were subjected to structural prediction, membrane-binding analysis, protein-DNA docking, protein-peptide docking, and Normal Mode Analysis. Protein-DNA docking identified the functional DNA-binding residues of DnaA, while peptide docking demonstrated that all four peptides interacted within this region. Peptide 3 exhibited the strongest predicted interaction, with a binding energy of -61.8+/-5.1, a buried surface area of 1151.7+/-30.8 A(2), and seven hydrogen bonds with key DnaA residues. Normal Mode Analysis further supported the structural stability of the peptide-protein complexes. These findings identify four promising AMP candidates targeting DnaA and provide a computational framework for peptide prioritization against multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae. However, the proposed interactions remain computational predictions and require experimental validation.
abstract_zh: 多重耐药肺炎克雷伯菌（Klebsiella pneumoniae）的迅速出现显著降低了传统抗生素的有效性，凸显了对替代治疗策略的需求。本研究采用综合性的计算机模拟流程，以识别靶向必需DNA复制起始蛋白DnaA的抗菌肽（antimicrobial peptides, AMPs）。从公开可用的AMP数据库中收集了共28,361条肽序列，并基于肽长度、净电荷、GRAVY评分、不稳定指数、抗菌活性、毒性、溶血潜力、聚集倾向、序列相似性及有利的两亲性特性进行顺序筛选。四条肽满足所有筛选标准，并进行了结构预测、膜结合分析、蛋白-DNA对接、蛋白-肽对接及简正模式分析。蛋白-DNA对接识别了DnaA的功能性DNA结合残基，而肽对接表明所有四条肽均在该区域内发生相互作用。肽3表现出最强的预测相互作用，结合能为-61.8±5.1，埋藏表面积为1151.7±30.8 Å²，并与关键DnaA残基形成七个氢键。简正模式分析进一步支持了肽-蛋白复合物的结构稳定性。这些发现识别出四种靶向DnaA的有前景的AMP候选物，并为针对多重耐药肺炎克雷伯菌的肽优先级排序提供了计算框架。然而，所提出的相互作用仍为计算预测，需实验验证。
